linkedIssues.title: MongoBackupRestoreIT: the Mongo container stops during startup on the CI runners
linkedIssues.description:
MongoBackupRestoreIT fails on the GitHub Actions runners, almost always now, and blocks every pull request into develop (the ruleset requires verify).
Failure: MongoBackupRestoreIT.requireClientBinariesAndAuthenticatedMongo (MongoBackupRestoreIT.java:110). The mongo:8.0.32 container (pinned by digest in #54) stops while the readiness probe waits for the final server: "Status 409: container <id> is not running". The assertion then prints "(container not running)" instead of the container log, so the reason is not captured.
Since 2026-10-20, 8 of 13 CI runs failed this way, develop included (da64901 "chore: open 1.2.0-SNAPSHOT", run 39393772456). On 2026-11-01 PR #52 failed it 3 times out of 3 on 12c05d6 (run 41325439727, attempts 1 to 3, 16:16 to 16:30 UTC). The same image runs normally on a developer machine (Docker 29.6.2) for over 35 seconds, so it is specific to the runners, as 8.0.34 was before (see the comment above IMAGE).
Next steps: keep the container log and exit code when it stops (the logs of an exited container can still be read before it is removed), find why the runner kills or stops mongod, then run the test on CI again. Until then it is skipped on GitHub Actions only.

record.title: fix(web): turn away an address after repeated failed sign-ins
reasons: AI marked it a security change

neutralSummary.whatChanged: dbvault now blocks sign-in attempts from an address after 10 failed attempts within 15 minutes, returning an error and requiring a wait before retrying.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: To prevent repeated failed sign-in attempts from the same address, reducing the risk of password guessing attacks.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: After 10 failed sign-ins from one address in 15 minutes, further attempts from that address are blocked for 15 minutes. The console shows an error message, and the API returns HTTP 429 with Retry-After. The limit and lockout duration can be configured with DBVAULT_SIGN_IN_MAX_FAILURES and DBVAULT_SIGN_IN_LOCK. The count resets on successful sign-in. The mechanism is in-memory, so a server restart clears the counts. If a proxy does not forward client addresses, all clients may be locked out together.
neutralSummary.migrationStep: We recommend also rate-limiting POST /login at your reverse proxy.
neutralSummary.limitations: Behind a proxy that doesn't forward the client address, every client shares one address and is locked out together. The counts live in memory, so a restart forgets them.

audienceNarratives.aut_r4_probe: After 10 failed sign-ins from one address in 15 minutes, dbvault blocks further attempts from that address for 15 minutes. Customers will see an error message or HTTP 429. Advise customers to check their network setup if they are unexpectedly locked out, especially if behind a proxy. Suggest configuring the new environment variables and adding rate limiting at the reverse proxy.
audienceNarratives.contributor: A new in-memory rate limiter blocks sign-in attempts from an address after 10 failures in 15 minutes. The limits are configurable via DBVAULT_SIGN_IN_MAX_FAILURES and DBVAULT_SIGN_IN_LOCK. The mechanism is shared between the console and API, and resets on successful sign-in. Tests added in SignInThrottleTest, SecurityConfigTest, and ApiSecurityTest.
audienceNarratives.dba: After 10 failed sign-ins from one address in 15 minutes, further attempts are blocked for 15 minutes. No changes to stored data or schema, but DBAs should ensure proxies forward client addresses to avoid accidental lockouts.
audienceNarratives.end_user: If you enter the wrong password too many times, you will need to wait 15 minutes before trying again. This helps protect your account.
audienceNarratives.operator: After 10 failed sign-ins from one address in 15 minutes, that address is blocked for 15 minutes. Configure DBVAULT_SIGN_IN_MAX_FAILURES and DBVAULT_SIGN_IN_LOCK as needed. Ensure your reverse proxy forwards client addresses to avoid locking out all users. Counts are in-memory and reset on server restart.
audienceNarratives.support: If a customer is locked out after too many failed sign-ins, explain that the system blocks further attempts from their address for 15 minutes. Advise checking proxy settings if multiple users are affected, and recommend configuring the new environment variables or adding rate limiting at the reverse proxy.

dba.headline: Sign-in lockout after repeated failures may affect access
dba.body: After 10 failed sign-ins from one address in 15 minutes, further attempts are blocked for 15 minutes. No changes to stored data or schema, but DBAs should ensure proxies forward client addresses to avoid accidental lockouts.

end_user.headline: Too many failed sign-ins will temporarily block your address
end_user.body: If you enter the wrong password too many times, you will need to wait 15 minutes before trying again. This helps protect your account.

operator.headline: Sign-in rate limiting by address; check proxy configuration and environment variables
operator.body: After 10 failed sign-ins from one address in 15 minutes, that address is blocked for 15 minutes. Configure DBVAULT_SIGN_IN_MAX_FAILURES and DBVAULT_SIGN_IN_LOCK as needed. Ensure your reverse proxy forwards client addresses to avoid locking out all users. Counts are in-memory and reset on server restart.

support.headline: Sign-in lockout after repeated failures: what to tell customers
support.body: If a customer is locked out after too many failed sign-ins, explain that the system blocks further attempts from their address for 15 minutes. Advise checking proxy settings if multiple users are affected, and recommend configuring the new environment variables or adding rate limiting at the reverse proxy.

record.title: feat(ui): show times in a time zone chosen in the sidebar (DBV-48)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The console now allows users to display times in a time zone of their choice, selectable from the sidebar.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: This change addresses the need for operators in different time zones to view times in their local zone, avoiding manual conversions.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: A new 'Time zone' option appears in the sidebar; selecting a zone and applying it updates all displayed times (backups, restores, verifications, retention runs, connection checks) to that zone, with the zone name shown. The choice is stored in a browser cookie and can also be set via the ?tz=<zone> URL parameter. This setting is browser-specific and not tied to the user account. Schedules retain their own time zones, and the HTTP API, CLI, and logs remain in UTC. Labels are available in English and Vietnamese.

neutralSummary.whatChanged: Backup sizes just under a unit boundary are shown in the next unit: 1,048,575 bytes is now 1.0 MB instead of 1024.0 KB.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: The size was rounded after its unit was chosen, so a value that rounds up to 1024 stayed in the smaller unit.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: `ByteSizes.readable` moves to the next unit from 1023.95 of the current one, so the rounded value never reads 1024.0; `ByteSizesTest` covers both sides of the boundary.

record.title: fix(restore): say when the backup a restore came from was deleted (DBV-49)

neutralSummary.whatChanged: The Restores list now displays 'Backup deleted since' when the source backup of a restore has been deleted, instead of showing a dash.
neutralSummary.whyChanged: Previously, a deleted source backup showed only a dash, which looked like missing data and confused users; this clarifies the situation.
neutralSummary.technicalDetail: The From backup column in the Restores list checks if the source backup still exists; if not, it displays a message indicating deletion, with translations for English and Vietnamese.

linkedIssues.title: Restores list: a deleted source backup shows as a bare dash
linkedIssues.description:
On Restores, a restore whose source backup was deleted afterwards (by retention, or by hand) shows only a dash in the From backup column. It reads as missing data, and an operator cannot tell whether the backup is gone or the page failed to load it.
Expected: the column says the backup was deleted since.
